purpose: This medication is used to treat a condition called cervical dystonia, which causes painful, involuntary muscle contractions in your neck that make your head twist or tilt into uncomfortable positions. It helps relax those overactive muscles so you can move more comfortably and with less pain. Your doctor injects it directly into the affected muscles.
how_it_works: RimabotulinumtoxinB is a purified protein made from a bacterium called Clostridium botulinum. When injected into a muscle, it blocks the nerve signals that tell the muscle to contract, causing the muscle to relax. Think of it like pressing a pause button on the nerve-to-muscle communication, which reduces those unwanted, painful spasms.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include dry mouth, difficulty swallowing, upset stomach, injection site pain, headache, neck pain, and feeling generally weak or tired. Dry mouth tends to be more common with this type of botulinum toxin compared to others.
warnings: There is a serious risk that the toxin can spread beyond the injection site to other parts of the body, which can cause symptoms like trouble swallowing, speaking, or breathing — this can be life-threatening. Tell your doctor right away if you notice any of these symptoms after your injection. Let your doctor know about all other medications you take, especially antibiotics or muscle relaxers, as they can increase your risk of serious side effects.
typical_dosing: This medication is given by injection directly into the neck muscles by a trained healthcare provider, usually in a clinic or doctor's office. The typical starting dose ranges from 2,500 to 5,000 units, divided among the affected muscles. Injections are usually repeated every 12 to 16 weeks, or as your doctor recommends based on how well you respond.
